newsitem.title: UK: HSBC up as Kleinwort rates "buy".
newsitem.headline: HSBC up as Kleinwort rates "buy".

text.p: Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc hit a record high on Friday amid further reaction to Monday's results and as analysts at Kleinwort Benson issued a strong "buy" on the stock and a 19.00 valuation, dealers said.
Despite a decline in its shares in Hong Kong -- where half its shares are owned -- HSBC shares were up 19-1/2p at 16.16 stg by 1130 GMT in volume of 3.0 million shares.
Earlier it rose as high as 16.19 stg, surpassing its previous peak of 16.00 stg set on Thursday.
Analysts at Kleinwort were not immediately avaiable for comment.
Dealers said there was general investment interest in the Anglo-Hong Kong banking group, which on Monday posted a 23 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profit to 4.52 billion stg.
"We just think it is the only growth bank in the UK," said one market-maker in HSBC shares. "I wouldn't be surprised to see it hit 20.00 stg this year."
Separately analysts at Lehman Brothers said HSBC's growth prospects could imply a 24.00 valuation and also repeated a "buy" on the shares.
"We believe HSBC is capable of sustaining its current 20 percent-plus return on equity in addition to double-figure volume growth," said Lehman analyst Robert Law in a research note.

"This combination would imply annualised returns of 14.6 percent in constant currency at the current price-to-book multiple of 2.7 times. A blended cost of equity of say 13 percent would imply a 24.00 stg share price," Law said.
Lehman forecasts a rise in pre-tax profit to 4.85 billion stg in 1997 and 5.45 billion in 1998.
